title: HCLTech’s $1.14 Billion Mercedes-Benz Deal Lifts Indian IT Stocks Amid Mixed Q1 Earnings
excerpt: India’s third-largest IT exporter snatched the mega-deal from rival Infosys, while the broader Q1 FY27 earnings season delivered sharply divergent results across the sector.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • HCLTech secured a $1.14 billion deal with Mercedes-Benz, boosting its shares by 6.3%.
  • Q1 FY27 results varied: HCLTech and TCS exceeded estimates, while Wipro fell short in revenue and profit.
  • HCLTech's AI revenue soared 62% year-on-year, but its FY27 growth guidance remained unchanged at 1-4%.
  • The Nifty IT index dropped 23% in 2026, reflecting concerns over AI disruption and weak spending.

HCLTech announcement and market reactions
  • HCLTech won a $1.14 billion AI-driven operating model contract from Mercedes-Benz, its first mega-deal in three years, boosting the Nifty IT index by 2.7% and HCLTech shares by 6.3%.
  • Q1 FY27 results split the sector: HCLTech, TCS, and Tech Mahindra beat revenue estimates, while Wipro missed on revenue, profit, and margin, with deal wins falling to $3.37 billion from $5 billion a year ago.
  • HCLTech’s advanced AI revenue surged 62% year-on-year to $171 million, but its unchanged FY27 guidance of 1–4% constant-currency growth disappointed analysts expecting an upgrade.
  • The Nifty IT index has fallen roughly 23% in 2026 as AI disruption fears and weak discretionary spending continue to weigh on India’s $315 billion IT industry.

HCLTech’s announcement on July 3 that it had won a $1.14 billion contract with a “Europe-headquartered, Fortune Global 50 firm” sent Indian IT stocks sharply higher and briefly revived a sector that has struggled through most of 2026. The deal, later reported by Livemint to be with Mercedes-Benz, was snatched from rival Infosys and marks HCLTech’s first mega-deal — valued above $1 billion — in three years.

HCLTech shares surged 6.3% on the BSE following the announcement, pulling the Nifty IT index up 2.7%. US-listed ADRs of Infosys and Wipro also rose as much as 4%, as investors bet the deal signalled a revival in large-contract activity for India’s IT outsourcing giants, according to NDTV Profit.

The Mercedes-Benz Contract

Under the five-and-a-half-year agreement, extendable by another five years, HCLTech will build an AI-driven operating model to transform and manage Mercedes-Benz’s global digital workplace and enterprise networks. The contract includes IT procurement — supplying the German carmaker’s employees with hardware and software across laptops and servers, according to people familiar with the matter cited by Livemint.

The deal is entirely net-new business, not a renewal. It assures HCLTech roughly $228 million in annual revenue, translating to about 1.6% growth in FY27. That incremental revenue is approximately the same amount Infosys lost when Mercedes-Benz sought new IT vendors following execution delays on an original $3.2 billion Daimler contract signed in December 2020.

“The deal strengthens HCLTech’s credibility in large-scale competitive pursuits at a time when enterprises are consolidating strategic technology partners.”

— Phil Fersht, CEO, HFS Research

Q1 FY27: A Split Verdict

The mega-deal set the tone for a Q1 FY27 earnings season that delivered starkly different outcomes across India’s top IT firms.

HCLTech itself posted a 13.9% year-on-year rise in revenue to ₹34,579 crore ($3.62 billion) for the April–June quarter, beating analysts’ estimates of ₹34,350 crore. Net profit climbed 20.3% to ₹4,624 crore. New deal bookings hit $2.4 billion, up from $1.9 billion the previous quarter and $1.8 billion a year earlier. Its advanced AI revenue — services like agentic AI and AI engineering — grew to $171 million, up 62.1% year-on-year in constant-currency terms, according to Reuters.

TCS, India’s largest IT firm, also beat quarterly revenue estimates. Tech Mahindra delivered an all-round beat with constant-currency revenue growing 3% quarter-on-quarter to $1.66 billion and deal wins of $1.1 billion, up 33% year-on-year. Brokerages including Nomura and Nuvama raised their target prices on Tech Mahindra.

Wipro was the clear underperformer. Revenue of ₹24,479 crore ($2.54 billion) missed the consensus estimate of ₹24,776 crore. Net profit inched up just 0.6% to ₹3,352 crore. Operating margin slipped to 16% from 17.3% in both the prior quarter and a year earlier, dragged down by salary hikes and large-deal ramp-up costs. Total deal wins fell sharply to $3.37 billion from $5 billion a year ago.

“Wipro is lagging its peers. It’s possible that the type of legacy deals that Wipro has is not able to generate sustaining growth.”

— Piyush Pandey, Senior Vice President, Centrum Broking

Despite the strong bookings, HCLTech’s decision to maintain its FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance at 1–4% disappointed markets. Shares fell 4.5% on July 14, wiping $1.54 billion from its market capitalisation. J.P. Morgan retained its “underweight” rating, citing continued weakness in discretionary spending and pressure in telecom and manufacturing accounts. Jefferies called the unchanged outlook “the key disappointment.”

CEO C. Vijayakumar acknowledged some impact from the West Asia conflict and softness in discretionary spend, but pointed to a large pipeline and healthy bookings. The company also signed a seven-year AI partnership with The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America to accelerate AI-led modernisation across the insurer’s operations.

Adding to sector jitters, IBM’s weak preliminary second-quarter results on July 14 — which sent its shares down over 25% — dragged Infosys ADR down 3% and Wipro ADR down 1.8%, as investors feared AI-driven shifts in enterprise spending could squeeze traditional IT services providers.

The AI Paradox for Indian IT

The earnings season crystallised what analysts call the AI paradox facing India’s IT sector. HCLTech’s AI revenue is growing rapidly and its mega-deal centred on AI-driven transformation. But investors worry that advanced AI tools could automate much of the work that Indian IT firms handle for global clients, disrupting business models across the $315 billion industry.

The Nifty IT index has fallen roughly 23% in 2026 — far steeper than the 7% decline in the Nifty 50 benchmark — reflecting these structural concerns alongside weak discretionary technology spending by global clients.

For Indian professionals working in or adjacent to the IT services industry overseas, the sector’s trajectory has direct implications. The shift toward AI-native capabilities may reshape hiring patterns and the skills premium for technology workers on H-1B and L-1 visas, even as mega-deals like the Mercedes-Benz win demonstrate that large-scale outsourcing contracts remain viable.

What’s Next

Infosys and Wipro are expected to report detailed quarterly results in coming weeks, with all eyes on deal pipelines and AI-related revenue disclosures. Wipro guided for Q2 revenue of $2.57–$2.63 billion, implying a 1.5% decline to 0.5% growth — a cautious outlook that reinforces concerns about uneven demand recovery. The HCLTech–Mercedes-Benz deal, meanwhile, marks Indian IT’s first mega-deal of FY27 and only the fourth since January 2024, suggesting that while billion-dollar contracts remain scarce, they have not dried up entirely.
